questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: That it was an English speaking country and that it was located near beautiful nature and mountains

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was not so easy and it took a lot of effort

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I was assisted to my room and they arranged social events in the beginning. I did not get a lot of help but I new where to seek help if I needed it.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Dorms of different sizes. I lived in an apartment with one other girl. We shared kitchen and bathroom but had own bedrooms. It was also an option to live 3 or 4 together.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: You could buy meal plans at the dining center but apartments also had a kitchen with cooking facilities

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It's easy to get to or from lectures and exercises. Everything is close by and campus has a lot of facilities such as gym, pool, squash courts and other sport facilities and a library. On the other hand you are more isolated from the rest of the city and you don't really need to go there.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Difficult to figure out a new system in the beginning but you get used to it

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could always ask for help

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: It took a lot of time to find suitable courses because some of them had restrictions regarding exchange students and all the courses had to fit together. It was a puzzle. I ended up changing a lot of the courses when I arrived at the university.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: You can always change courses in the first few weeks of the semester, so if you don't like the courses you chose beforehand or if it is inconvenient for you, you can change courses when you arrive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of the courses were very different. Some of them were difficult others were easy. The 200 level courses were very easy and not a huge workload whereas courses at a 400 level requires more work.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Very different. I had a bigger workload during the semester with more assignments and presentations than on UCPH which also counted in the final grade. I also had midterms in Canada, so overall more preparation during the semester at my host institution than on UCPH .

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Introduction to Geology, Global Food Politics and Sustainability and Political Ecology

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Global Food Politics. Very nice teacher and the course has a good structure

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: transportation. Public transportation is not good in Canada so I used a lot of money on renting cars to get around.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: groceries were more expensive than expected. I think more or less everything was more expensive than expected.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Almost everything. The university had all sorts of clubs that you could engage in. Both cultural, social, athletic and academic clubs. This was very good!

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Sport because it is always fun to do together and the university had a lot of 'free' facilities.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to Rocky Mountains. I used many weekends in the mountains and it is very beautiful. I never got tired of it and you can hike in the summer and ski in the winter :D

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: People were very nice and welcoming so that made it easier but it is a challenge in the beginning

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: the local students are open to socializing with international and exchange students but if you are living with locals it is easier

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: not anything specific but adjusting to a different school system and speaking another language

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: the very friendly approach they had to foreigners which is very different from Denmark

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Find out what works for you <3

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: no

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Living in another country so far away for a longer period and being in the nature with good friends

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: the school system

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: no

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
